subject: Archaeology
subcategory: Lost Cities of the Ancient World
title: Dunhuang: The Silk Road Oasis
description: A 60-second lesson on Dunhuang: The Silk Road Oasis.

hook.text: A Taoist monk stumbled into a sealed cave in China and found 50,000 ancient documents hidden inside.

buildup.text: Dunhuang was a key Silk Road stop. Buddhist monks carved 492 caves into the cliffs and filled them with art.

discovery.text: The Library Cave, sealed around 1000 CE, contained the world's oldest printed book — the Diamond Sutra from 868 CE.

twist.text: British explorer Aurel Stein bought thousands of manuscripts for a tiny fee. China calls it cultural theft.

climax.text: The documents are now split between London, Paris, Beijing, and St. Petersburg. No single place holds them all.

punchline.text: A monk opened a cave. The world's oldest printed book fell out.

quiz.question: What was found in the sealed Library Cave at Dunhuang?
options: Thousands of jade artifacts from the Han Dynasty
50,000 documents including the world's oldest printed book
Silk garments preserved in perfect condition

details.summary: Dunhuang, an oasis city on China's Silk Road, is famous for the Mogao Caves — nearly 500 cave temples carved from the 4th to 14th centuries, containing the world's finest collection of Buddhist art, manuscripts, and the oldest known printed book, the Diamond Sutra of 868 CE.
details.whyItMatters: Dunhuang's sealed Library Cave, discovered in 1900, contained over 50,000 manuscripts in multiple languages — the greatest single manuscript discovery in history.
takeaways: Nearly 500 cave temples carved from the 4th to 14th centuries
The Library Cave contained over 50,000 manuscripts sealed since 1000 CE
Home to the world's oldest known printed book — the Diamond Sutra

faq.question: How was the Library Cave at Dunhuang discovered?
faq.answer: In 1900, a Taoist monk named Wang Yuanlu discovered a hidden sealed chamber containing tens of thousands of manuscripts, paintings, and textiles deposited before the cave was sealed around 1000 CE.

faq.question: Why is the Diamond Sutra significant?
faq.answer: Dated to 868 CE, it is the oldest known complete printed book. It demonstrates that woodblock printing was already a mature technology in China centuries before Gutenberg. The scroll is 5 meters long and features a detailed frontispiece illustration, showing sophisticated printing capabilities.
